dedupe_keys.name: pignoletto open source web platform for gis soil data management and analytics precision agriculture

description: Pignoletto is a web platform for collecting, visualising, managing and analysing soil data for precision agriculture, described in an open-access article in Sensors in April 2023. It takes heterogeneous data from proximity sensors on the ground, airborne and spaceborne sources, lets users add new data, including measurements uploaded straight from the acquisition device, and lets them plug in their own predictive models to map soil properties such as nutrients, moisture and texture. It is built from open-source components, with Lizmap publishing QGIS projects through QGIS Server, and the code is available online as Docker containers. It was developed by Flavio Piccoli, Simone Giuseppe Locatelli, Raimondo Schettini and Paolo Napoletano at the University of Milano-Bicocca and the National Institute for Nuclear Physics in Milan, and tested within the Pignoletto project, an Italian project on land monitoring tools. The article is free under CC BY 4.0; the software licence is not stated in it. Caveats: it was tested on one project area, the usability experiments were small, and no activity after 2023 was checked, so maturity is unknown. For simulation it offers a template for a farm-scale spatial data layer that feeds soil and crop models and field-level digital twins. It is related to the precision agriculture tools plugin for QGIS record in this catalogue.
